idiom_name: pointfreeco/swift-snapshot-testing assertSnapshot(of:as:) with recorded reference files
implementation_notes: XCTest and swift-testing provide runners and assertions but no baseline store, and the ecosystem's de-facto realization is swift-snapshot-testing: assertSnapshot(of:as:) serializes a value (or renders a view to an image) into a reference file that is compared on later runs, snapshot(record:) controls re-recording, and the library also offers inline snapshot testing for small values that should live in the source. That replaces the hand-written read/compare/update path; writing it yourself is only worth it when the artefact is produced outside the test process or when no dependency is acceptable. Snapshot recording must be a deliberate local act, never a side effect of a CI run.
pitfalls: Recording mode is context-dependent (the record parameter and CI detection); leaving it at record: .all in a pipeline silently rewrites every baseline.
Image snapshots depend on device, OS version, simulator and scale factor and are pixel-fragile; pin the traits and consider a perceptual tolerance for anti-aliasing.
Reference directories must be part of the test target's resources (and survive Xcode's file-system synchronisation rules) or the snapshot cannot be read from the sandboxed test bundle.
